canada.title: Hearing on controversial plans to export power from Powell River to U.S. wraps up
canada.summary: An unprecedented federal hearing for an independent power producer's application to export all its electricity from a small B.C. community to the U.S. for 30 years wrapped up on Friday, after arguments from the company and local intervenors opposed to the deal.

canada.title: Edmonton community league, skateboarding group upset after city destroys ‘unauthorized additions’ at skatepark
canada.summary: The City of Edmonton has demolished part of a skatepark in the North Glenora neighbourhood, upsetting leaders from the community league and skateboarding community, who say the area was a unique gathering spot.

canada.title: Gander resident Matthew Collins faces charges related to alleged bomb making
canada.summary: Matthew Collins, who lives in Gander, is facing eight charges. They include possessing explosives and prohibited weapons, uttering threats and intimidation by using violence.

canada.title: 'We are sorry': Rocks found in restaurant burritos in Alberta
canada.summary: BarBurrito issued an apology to its customers after pea-sized stones were found in some of its burritos at restaurants in Alberta. The company says the rocks came from a particular brand of beans that it is no longer using.

canada.title: Staples Canada says customer information accessed in data breach
canada.summary: Staples Canada says hackers accessed customer information in a cyberattack this month.

canada.title: Ontario Liberals to name new leader after weeks of voting, months of campaigning
canada.summary: Ontario Liberals are getting ready to name their new party leader, with results from members’ ranked ballots set to be revealed later today.

canada.title: From the ISS to the Yukon: Whitehorse students ask astronauts about space
canada.summary: Canadian astronauts Jenni Gibbons and Joshua Kutryk — who lived in Yukon as a kid — spoke to students from several schools this week. Gibbons was in Whitehorse, while Kutryk was aboard the International Space Station.

canada.title: A year ago, her daughter died of a toxic drug overdose. Now, she's pushing for change
canada.summary: Tara Marshall wants stronger mandatory minimum sentences for repeat and bulk drug traffickers, after the death of her daughter Kennedy Grace Crowe.

canada.title: Woman's airport security ordeal with dad's ashes highlights challenges of travelling with cremated remains
canada.summary: Rules around transporting creamated remains through airports and challenges with new scanners can add "another layer of grief" to an already stressful time, says the head of the Funeral Service Association of Canada.

canada.title: Judge awards damages to both sides in lawsuit after neighbours' dispute over loose dogs 'spun out of control'
canada.summary: A judge has awarded an eastern Manitoba couple sued by their neighbour $10,000 in damages, and their neighbour $1,000, after an "unfortunate series of events" unfolded over dogs allowed to run loose on an unfenced property.

canada.title: N.B. publisher of Giller Prize-winning novel says win proves important stories can come out of the Maritimes
canada.summary: Susanne Alexander, the publisher at Goose Lane Editions, said Nicholas Herring was a dark horse in the running for the Giller Prize. When he won, she was ecstatic.

canada.title: Big Brothers Big Sisters launches 'Start Small' campaign to recruit more male mentors
canada.summary: Some boys in Atlantic Canada are waiting nearly two years for a mentor as Big Brothers Big Sisters faces a sharp shortage of male volunteers across its 12 regional agencies.

canada.title: Q&A | Inuvik mayor hopes defence investments allow for 'legacy projects'
canada.summary: The Department of National Defence is set to spend hundreds of millions of dollars in Inuvik, N.W.T., to expand the airport and build one of the military's new forward operating bases. Mayor Peter Clarkson joined CBC's The Trailbreaker to talk about what these investments mean for the town.

canada.title: Rohingya 'clearance operation' survivor in N.L. triumphant following genocide ruling
canada.summary: Muhammad Rofique of St. John's is celebrating, but still reflecting upon the atrocities he lived through in Myanmar as the world’s highest court declares the country committed genocide against his people.

canada.title: Quebec's popular PEQ program is closed — again. People counting on it want answers
canada.summary: The popular immigration pathway known as the PEQ was temporarily revived earlier this year. The first period for applications was open between July 2 and Oct. 31, and it's not clear when the Quebec government will open a second window for applicants.
